At a 0.20 probability threshold, the model achieved 93.67% precision and 77.89% recall, detecting 74 of 95 fraudulent transactions while generating only 5 false alerts.\n\nFrom a financial perspective, the model detected approximately 72.71% of the fraudulent transaction value in the test set.\n\nThe project demonstrates how machine learning predictions can be translated into practical fraud-risk and financial decision-making.","metadata":{}},{"cell_type":"markdown","source":"## Project Objective\n\nThe objective is to develop a fraud detection workflow that answers three business questions:\n\n1. Which transaction patterns are associated with fraudulent activity?\n2. Which classification approach provides useful fraud detection performance?\n3. How does changing the detection threshold affect fraud detection, false alerts, and financial exposure?\n\nThe goal is not simply to maximize prediction accuracy, but to find a practical balance between detecting fraud and controlling unnecessary alerts.","metadata":{}},{"cell_type":"markdown","source":"We import the libraries needed for data manipulation, numerical analysis, and visualization. imbalanced, with fraudulent transactions representing only a small fraction of total transactions.\n- Random Forest achieved a PR-AUC of approximately **0.806**, indicating strong fraud-ranking performance on the imbalanced dataset.\n- At the selected **0.20 probability threshold**, the model achieved **93.67% precision**, **77.89% recall**, and an **85.06% F1-score**.\n- The model identified **74 of 95 fraudulent transactions**, while generating only **5 false alerts**.\n- The detected fraudulent transactions represented approximately **72.71% of the total fraudulent transaction value** in the test set.\n- The model detected approximately **$10,736** in fraudulent transaction value while approximately **$4,030** of fraudulent value was missed.\n- False alerts represented approximately **$1,121** in transaction value.\n\n### Business Interpretation\n\nThe analysis shows that fraud detection should not be evaluated using accuracy alone. Because fraudulent transactions are rare, precision, recall, PR-AUC, and financial exposure provide a more meaningful assessment.\n\nThe probability threshold also has a direct business impact. Lowering the threshold can increase fraud detection but may generate more false alerts, while increasing it can reduce alerts at the cost of missing more fraud.\n\nThe selected **0.20 threshold** provides a practical operating point for this analysis, combining high precision with substantial fraud recall while keeping false alerts low.\n\n### Final Takeaway\n\nThis project demonstrates an end-to-end fraud analytics workflow: data quality checks, exploratory analysis, feature analysis, model comparison, threshold optimization, error analysis, and financial impact assessment.\n\nThe key objective is not simply to build a model that predicts fraud, but to translate model predictions into **risk and financial decisions**.","metadata":{}}]}
